facts.text: Van Cortlandt Manor House, located at 525 South Riverside Avenue, sits on a portion of the original 86,000‑acre tract granted by King William III to Stephanus Van Cortlandt in 1697.
The manor house was built around 1732 by Philip Van Cortlandt and became a permanent residence when his son Pierre moved in 1749.
In 1961, Van Cortlandt Manor was registered as a National Historic Landmark, and the house itself was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.
The Albany Post Road ran through the property, making the manor a crucial stop between New York City and Albany after the Revolutionary War.
The original 86,000‑acre estate was divided among Stephanus’s ten heirs after his death in 1700, leading to the breakup of the massive property.
Cortlandt Manor derives its name from the Van Cortlandt family, one of six manors that split Westchester County before the Revolutionary War.
